knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

### Data Loading

```{r Data Loading}

library(tidyverse)

#Load in Data
ehr_data <- read_csv("final_readmission_cohort.csv")

#double check data load
glimpse(ehr_data)
```

### Convert Variables to Factors and Create a Summary Table

```{r Convert Variables to Factors and Create a Summary Table}

#Convert binary and categorical variables into factors
ehr_clean <- ehr_data %>%
  mutate(
    is_30d_readmission = as.factor(is_30d_readmission),
    GENDER = as.factor(gender),
    COUNTY = as.factor(county),
    CITY = as.factor(city),
    DIAGNOSIS = as.factor(primary_diagnosis)
  )

#Summary of data with variables as factor
summary(ehr_clean)
```

### Summary Table with Gender and Demography

```{r Summary Table with Gender and Demography}

## Summary Table with Gender and Demography

library(gtsummary)

#Build the stratified summary table
ehr_clean %>%
  #Select the specific columns in the summary
  select(age_at_admission, GENDER, COUNTY, procedure_count, length_of_stay, is_30d_readmission) %>%
  #Group by if they were readmitted
  tbl_summary(by = is_30d_readmission) %>%
  #Add p-values to compare
  add_p()
```


### Top 15 Clinical Drivers of Readmission Graph

```{r Top 15 Clinical Drivers of Readmission Graph, fig.width=5, fig.height=3.5, fig.align="center"}
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)

#Top 15 Clinical Drivers of Readmission
ehr_clean %>%
  #Step 1: Filter for patients who were readmitted
  filter(is_30d_readmission == "1") %>%
  
  #Step 2: Remove missing data and NULL
  drop_na(DIAGNOSIS) %>%
  filter(DIAGNOSIS != "NULL") %>%
  
  #Step 3: Filter out Social Health determinants and administrative noise
  filter(!str_detect(str_to_lower(DIAGNOSIS), "review|employment|labor|social|violence|finding|situation|routine|normal")) %>%
  
  #Step 4: Count the number of occurrences of each specific diagnosis
  count(DIAGNOSIS, name = "readmission_count") %>%
  
  #Step 5: Keep only the top 15 most frequent conditions
  slice_max(order_by = readmission_count, n = 15) %>%
  
  #Step 6: Build the plot
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(DIAGNOSIS, readmission_count), y = readmission_count)) +
  geom_col(fill = "turquoise3") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 15 Clinical Drivers of 30-Day Readmissions",
    x = "Primary Diagnosis",
    y = "Total Number of Readmissions"
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) str_wrap(x, width = 30)) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Top 15 Social Drivers of Readmission Graph

```{r Top 15 Social Drivers of Readmission Graph}

#The Social Determinants Plot: Non-Clinical Drivers of Readmission
ehr_clean %>%
  #Step 1: Filter for patients who were readmitted
  filter(is_30d_readmission == "1") %>%
  
  #Step 2: Remove missing data and NULL
  drop_na(DIAGNOSIS) %>%
  filter(DIAGNOSIS != "NULL") %>%
  
  #Step 3: Drop the medication review (non clinical and not readmission)
  filter(!str_detect(str_to_lower(DIAGNOSIS), "medication review")) %>%
  
  #Step 4: Filter the social and administrative findings
  filter(str_detect(str_to_lower(DIAGNOSIS), "employment|labor|social|stress|finding|situation")) %>%
  
  #Step 5: Count and slice the top 15
  count(DIAGNOSIS, name = "readmission_count") %>%
  slice_max(order_by = readmission_count, n = 15) %>%
  
  #Step 6: Build the plot 
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(DIAGNOSIS, readmission_count), y = readmission_count)) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkorange") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 15 Social & Administrative Drivers of 30-Day Readmissions",
    x = "Social Determinant / Finding",
    y = "Total Number of Readmissions"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
### Highest Readmission Rate by County Graph

```{r Highest Readmission Rate by County Graph}

#Load the scales package to format our axis as percentages
library(scales)

ehr_clean %>%
  #Step 1: Remove missing county data
  drop_na(COUNTY) %>%
  
  #Step 2: Group the data by County
  group_by(COUNTY) %>%
  
  #Step 3: Calculate totals and relative frequencies (percentages)
  summarize(
    total_visits = n(),
    readmitted_count = sum(is_30d_readmission == "1"),
    readmission_rate = readmitted_count / total_visits
  ) %>%
  
  #Step 4: The Sample Size Filter
  #Drop any county with fewer than 30 total visits to eliminate statistical noise
  filter(total_visits >= 30) %>%
  
  #Step 5: Keep the top 15 counties with the highest readmission rates
  slice_max(order_by = readmission_rate, n = 15) %>%
  
  #Step 6: Build the plot
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(COUNTY, readmission_rate), y = readmission_rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = "slategray") +
  coord_flip() +
  
  #Format the Y-axis (which is flipped to the bottom) as percentages
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Highest 30-Day Readmission Rates by County",
    subtitle = "Filtered for counties with n >= 30 hospital visits",
    x = "County",
    y = "Relative Readmission Rate (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
### Logistic Regression Model

```{r Logistic Regression Model}

library(broom)

#Step 1: Build the Logistic Regression Model
#Testing if readmission is driven by Age and Gender
readmission_model <- glm(
  is_30d_readmission ~ age_at_admission + GENDER, 
  data = ehr_clean, 
  family = "binomial" #This tells R it's a Yes/No (1 or 0) outcome
)

#Step 2: Tidy the results and calculate the Odds Ratios with CI
tidy(readmission_model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
```
